This suit is filed by Late plaintiff Venkatachalappa.H.V., for the relief of declaration to declare that he is the absolute owner and possessor of the suit property.

He also sought declaration that the Sale Deeds mentioned in the prayer column are null and void not binding on the plaintiffs and also sought for permanent injunction.
2.
The brief facts of the case of the plaintiff's are as follows:-

Late plaintiff claimed that he is the owner and possessor of site No.17 in Sy.No.141 of village Kethumaranahalli, Yeshwanthapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk,
measuring East to West 30ft, North to South 26ft.
The Late plaintiff purchased the suit schedule property by virtue of Sale Deed, dated 08-10-1974.
According to the plaintiff, he paid betterment charges to BBMP on 13-08-1975.

The plaintiff claimed that the suit property consists of house and vacant site, an area of 19 ft x 29ft was sold by Late plaintiff Venkatachalappa in favour of Nagaraja, Nagaraja has sold the same to Krishnaiah Shetty.
After selling the said property, the plaintiff becomes owner to the extent of 26ft x 30ft.

sentences.text: Suits for declaration of title against the government differ from suits against private parties on two counts: a.

First, there is a presumption in favour of the Government in such suits, as all lands which are unoccupied or not vested in any individual or local authority, are presumed to belong exclusively to the Government.
b. Secondly, there is an additional burden of proof on the party seeking declaration of title against the Government.
The plaintiff has to establish its possession over the land in question for a period of thirty years as opposed to twelve years in the case of adverse possession against a private party.
ii. A decree declaring title against the Government must not be passed casually.

Before granting any such decree, the trial court must ensure that the plaintiff has furnished adequate documentary evidence, either through title deeds tracing ownership for over thirty years or by establishing adverse possession for a period of thirty years.
iii. The Trial Court must verify whether the name of the plaintiff has been recorded as the owner, holder, or occupant in the relevant revenue or municipal records for more than thirty years.

. Finally, the Trial Court must carefully scrutinize the nature of the possession as may be asserted, determining whether the same is authorized or unauthorized, permissive or casual, furtive or clandestine, as well as open,
continuous, and hostile, or implied by title, to ensure that public property is not inadvertently converted into private ownership by unscrupulous elements.
This decision is with respect to notice under Section 80 of CPC , but the same analogy applies to to Section 64 of BDA Act .
Therefore, on this ground also, the suit against the defendant No.1 is not maintainable.
The Court Fee is also not proper and sufficient as the plaintiff sought cancellation of sale deed, the falls under Section 38 of KCF and SV Act.

It reads thus:-
38. Suits for cancellation of decrees, etc.- (1) In a suit for cancellation of a decree for money or other property having a money value, or other document which purports or operates to create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish, whether in present or in future, any right, title or interest in money, movable or immovable property, fee shall be computed on the value of the subject-matter of the suit, and such value shall be deemed to be,--
if the whole decree or other document is sought to be cancelled, the amount or value of the property for which the decree was passed or other document was executed;
O.S.No.2411/2010 if a part of the decree or other document is sought to be cancelled, such part of the amount or value of the property.
The Court fee paid by the plaintiff is insufficient.
Hence, I answer issue Nos.1 to 4 in negative, issue Nos.5 to 7 in affirmative, issue No.8 in negative, issue No.9 in affirmative, issue No.10 in negative.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, the subsequent execution of the Sale Deeds by the vendor of the Late plaintiff has no sanctity in the eye of law.
Therefore, the vendors of Late plaintiff have no right to execute the Sale Deed in favour of plaintiff on 8-10-1974.
There is a Provisions in Bengaluru Development Authority Act for allotment of the sites but the said Provision is not utilized by the plaintiff and now, they are claiming the O.S.No.2411/2010 property belonging to the defendant No.4 as their property.
The Late plaintiff while he was in the Central Jail filed a complaint before the Lokayuktha, alleging that the BDA has allotting the sites belonging to him to others.
